# tls

OpenSSL helpers: inspect a certificate file, inspect a live endpoint, and generate self-signed certificates for local testing.

---

## `tls_gen_self_signed`

Generate a self-signed certificate, its key, and a concatenated PEM bundle (the form mongod and some proxies want) into a directory. With no output directory it creates a fresh private temp dir and prints the path. Never changes your working directory.

**Usage**

```sh
tls_gen_self_signed [common-name] [days] [output-dir]
```

**Examples**

```sh
tls_gen_self_signed
tls_gen_self_signed mongo.local 825 ~/certs
```

**Requires** `openssl`

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/tls.sh:54`](../../modules/common/tls.sh#L54)

## `tls_get_remote_info`

Print the notBefore/notAfter dates of the certificate a TLS server is currently presenting. SNI name and connect host are separate so you can test a specific backend behind a load balancer.

**Usage**

```sh
tls_get_remote_info [sni-name] [host] [port]
```

**Examples**

```sh
tls_get_remote_info example.com
tls_get_remote_info www.example.com 203.0.113.10 8443
```

**Requires** `openssl`

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/tls.sh:36`](../../modules/common/tls.sh#L36)

## `tls_show_cert`

Print a certificate file in full human-readable form: subject, issuer, validity window, SANs, key usage, signature algorithm.

**Usage**

```sh
tls_show_cert <certificate-file>
```

**Examples**

```sh
tls_show_cert /etc/ssl/certs/mycert.crt
```

**Requires** `openssl`

**OS** any &nbsp;·&nbsp; **Source** [`modules/common/tls.sh:13`](../../modules/common/tls.sh#L13)
